newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Lehman lowers Gilat EPS.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Lehman lowers Gilat EPS.

text.p: Lehman Brothers lowered its 1997 and 1998 earnings per share (EPS) estimates for Israel's Gilat Satellite Networks Ltd, citing increased interest expenses from amortising a convertible note offering.
Gilat last week said it had sold $75 million in 6.5 percent convertible subordinated notes in a private placement.

Lehman analyst Tim Luke said in a report released on Sunday Gilat was amortising the expenses of the convertible offering over a shorter time frame than initially calculated and would pay interest above an indicated mid-range of 6.0 percent.
"Our preliminary estimates which we view as conservative move from $1.58 and $2.01 in 1997 and 1998 to $1.50 and $1.90," Luke said.

Lehman said it maintained a 12-month price target of $45 as investors were likely to focus on Gilat's ability to deliver strong revenue and earnings growth of some 30 percent as it gained share in the expanding VSAT (very small aperture terminal) market and broadened its product portfolio.
The Tel Aviv-based company is trading at $30-5/8.
Gilat last week reported better-than-expected first quarter earnings of $0.28 against Lehman's consensus estimate of $0.27.
"Gilat's cash levels of approximately $20 million will now be augmented by the recent offering of $75 million in convertible subordinated notes," Luke said.

"We believe that near term Gilat is likely to direct some of the proceeds from its recent offering towards a new Global Village Phone rural telephony venture which could provide substantial incremental growth opportunities," he said.
Lehman maintains its 2-Outperform rating for Gilat.
